cards.title: A Semantic Model for Species Description Applied to the Ensign Wasps (Hymenoptera: Evaniidae) of New Caledonia
cards.lesson: Ensign wasps develop individually as predators of cockroach eggs inside egg cases. This supports the distinction between the adult wasp placing an egg and its developing young doing the feeding.

cards.title: What is a beneficial parasite?
cards.publisher: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service, Insects in the City
cards.lesson: Many insect parasitoids specialize on one or a few related host species. This explains why a natural enemy relationship should not be generalized to every pest or every wasp.
cards.species: Insect parasitoids in general; the article includes ensign wasps as an example
cards.region: Texas extension education with general garden and urban-landscape context
cards.limits: General parasitoid biology, not an Evania-specific host-range experiment. Do not transfer the general one-host description to individual cockroach eggs: an ensign larva eats several eggs in one case. Do not use the pesticide sections or imply reliable whole-home control.
